clinicalPearls: A distinctive multisystem disorder combining exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, hypoplasia of the nasal alae (nasal wings) and scalp aplasia cutis congenita
Autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in UBR1, a component of the ubiquitin-proteasome protein degradation pathway
Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency presents early with malabsorption, steatorrhoea and failure to thrive and requires pancreatic enzyme replacement and fat-soluble vitamin support
The characteristic facial appearance includes the hypoplastic, beak-like nasal alae with midline scalp defects
Sensorineural hearing loss is common and warrants early audiological assessment
Additional features include hypothyroidism, dental anomalies, growth failure, developmental delay of variable degree and genitourinary or anorectal malformations
Diabetes mellitus can develop over time as the endocrine pancreas becomes involved
Diagnosis rests on the recognisable pattern of malformations confirmed by UBR1 genetic testing
reference.pathophysiology: Johanson-Blizzard syndrome is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in UBR1, which encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase of the N-end rule pathway that targets specific proteins for degradation by the proteasome. Loss of UBR1 function disturbs regulated protein turnover, and the acinar cells of the exocrine pancreas are especially vulnerable, undergoing destruction and fatty or fibrotic replacement that produces early and severe exocrine pancreatic insufficiency. The same developmental disturbance affects craniofacial, ectodermal, endocrine and other structures, giving the hypoplastic nasal alae, aplasia cutis of the scalp, hearing loss, hypothyroidism, dental and genitourinary anomalies and variable developmental delay. Management is supportive, centred on enzyme replacement, nutrition and treatment of the associated endocrine and sensory deficits.
additionalDifferentials: Other syndromic causes of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
Other dysmorphic syndromes with aplasia cutis
additionalInvestigations: Faecal elastase and other tests of exocrine pancreatic function
Nutritional assessment with fat-soluble vitamin levels
Audiological evaluation for sensorineural hearing loss
Thyroid function tests and, over time, glucose monitoring for diabetes
Imaging and examination for genitourinary, anorectal and dental anomalies
redFlags: Severe malabsorption with faltering growth in infancy
Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency and its complications
reference.prognosis: With early pancreatic enzyme replacement, nutritional support and treatment of hypothyroidism and hearing loss, growth and development can improve; long-term outcome depends on the severity of malabsorption, endocrine involvement and any associated malformations and developmental impairment.
pitfalls: Confusing it with Shwachman-Diamond syndrome or cystic fibrosis and missing the characteristic dysmorphology
Overlooking sensorineural hearing loss that affects development
Failing to monitor for evolving hypothyroidism and diabetes
Under-treating exocrine insufficiency and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: Give pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy to correct exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, steatorrhoea and malabsorption
Supplement fat-soluble vitamins and provide dietetic-led nutritional support to restore growth
Treat associated hypothyroidism with levothyroxine replacement
Provide early audiological rehabilitation with hearing aids for sensorineural hearing loss
Undertake endocrine surveillance with glucose monitoring for later diabetes from progressive pancreatic disease
Arrange surgical correction of genitourinary and anorectal malformations and dedicated dental care
Offer developmental support and multidisciplinary follow-up
Provide autosomal recessive genetic counselling and family screening
